title: Paired states and Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite planar graphs
main_claim: Barnette's conjecture: every cubic bipartite planar 3-connected graph is Hamiltonian. This is proved through Theorem 2.2. Take any sphere triangulation whose faces are properly 2-coloured, and any face t0 with an edge e0 of it. Then the vertices split into two sets, each inducing a tree, with the ends of e0 in one set and the third vertex of t0 in the other. When there is no separating triangle, the proof runs as follows. A flow argument gives two disjoint states (Prop 3.1). A weighted exponential sum then shows that some pair (r,s) has Q_s a forest (Prop 4.1). In that sum, a sign-reversing involution, justified by the disk identity, cancels every pair whose Q_s has a cycle. Positive spoke circulations show the sum is nonzero, by looking at its leading Taylor coefficient. Plane-tree duality then gives one selected edge per face, and these edges form a forest with 2 components. Separating triangles are handled by induction, gluing the two pieces along the cap face where the prescription was set.

issues.location: Lemma 2.1 (duality) and Section 5.1 (faces of H correspond to the white triangles)
issues.description: Two arguments are very brief, but they are correct. Lemma 2.1 says contraction 'preserves faces' and leaves out the loop and multigraph bookkeeping. The match between the faces of H and the white triangles rests on a sector-merging sketch, although Euler's formula confirms the count: |V(H)|=2k+2, |E(H)|=3k, so H has k faces.
issues.evidence: I rechecked both with Euler counts. Neither affects correctness.

coverage:
I read the whole proof in paper.tex and checked each step by hand:
(1) Prop 3.1. The max-flow cut capacity, its reduction to the density bound e(U)-b(U) <= 2|U|-4, and the bound itself. The bound uses component faces of K, the region balance |b'-w'| <= d-4 (cases d=4, 5 and >=6), the fact that triangular faces of K are actual faces when there is no separating triangle, and the small-component bounds.
(2) Lemma 4.1, the disk identity. B+W = 2I+h-2, 3(B-W) = 2l-h and B = I+l together give 2l-h = -3.
(3) Lemma 4.3. The chosen cycle depends only on s, it must be directed, the swap is a fixed-point-free involution, and J changes by (2/3)(±3) = ±2.
(4) Lemma 4.4 and the nonvanishing argument. The face circulations are realizable, the spoke curve is simple and counterclockwise, each group has the product form (-i e^{xL+} + i e^{xL-}), and the leading coefficients all have phase (-i)^{c_min} times a positive number, so they cannot cancel.
(5) Section 5. Each component of Q_s contains exactly one root. H minus the s-spokes is a spanning tree. The white-face selection gives exactly one selected edge per face. P0 is acyclic because B-W = 2l-h is incompatible with 3(B-W) = 2l-h ≠ 0, and the white face y0 cannot lie inside the disk. The Jordan-curve labelling gives inducedness.
(6) Gluing at separating triangles. The cap colouring is forced, and the two trees intersect in a vertex or an edge. The final step from the partition to a Hamiltonian cycle (Theorem 1.1) also checks out.

Numerics: I built plantri and enumerated Eulerian triangulations with plantri -b.
- Brute force over all n <= 16: every face t0 and edge e0 admits the prescribed induced-tree partition, with no failures.
- Every triangulation with n <= 14 and no separating triangle, for every black outer face: pairs of states exist, J is always an integer, the i^J terms cancel exactly for every s with Q_s cyclic, and pairs with Q_s a forest always exist.

Not checked independently: the external equivalence from GSW2023 (Theorem 4.16) used in Corollary 6.2.
